description: Capability for the main window. The webview loads the dev-server UI from a loopback http://localhost:<port> origin, which Tauri treats as REMOTE content — so app commands (github_sign_in / github_is_signed_in / github_sign_out / github_open_verification) must opt that origin in via `remote.urls` (Phase 28 / DDR-108/109). The port is dynamic (4399→4401 on collision), hence the loopback wildcard. SECURITY: the untrusted cross-origin canvas iframe (a different localhost port) cannot invoke despite the wildcard match — and note it DOES match it, since wry passes the calling frame's own URL into the IPC request. Two things stop it, and the second is the load-bearing one: (a) core init scripts are injected `for_main_frame_only`, so the iframe never gets the Tauri JS global; (b) `window.webkit.messageHandlers.ipc` IS reachable from every frame, so what actually rejects the iframe is Webview::on_message dropping any invoke whose `invoke_key` doesn't match the per-run random key — which the iframe never receives. Leg (a) alone is one API call away from being wrong; leg (b) is the invariant. None of these commands return the token either (the token bridge is loopback HTTP + key, not a Tauri command). Verified in the DDR-109 security pass and re-verified in the 2026-08-04 defender pass. BROWSER OPENERS: `open_github_url` and `open_cloud_url` are the only two ways the webview reaches the OS browser, and NEITHER is a general opener (DDR-054 forbids one) — each is zone-locked in Rust, not by its argument. `open_cloud_url` resolves the allowed origin per call from MAUDE_CLOUD_URL (default https://cloud.maude.sh), exactly as the sidecar does, and accepts only that exact origin or an https host inside its zone; a self-hoster changing the env changes both halves together instead of leaving Rust locked to a stale origin.
